question: Has commissioning, compliant performance verification and operational handover of the new Willawarrin water treatment plant been completed?
why_exists: Council's live project page checked 22 September 2026 now states construction is nearing completion and the project has entered commissioning (EV-0099). It defines commissioning as mechanical, electrical and hydraulic testing before handover. This resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether commissioning had begun, but does not establish that commissioning, performance verification or handover is complete.
evidence_required_to_resolve: A current Council/NSW Government completion or handover notice, commissioning acceptance record, compliant water-quality/performance test result, or equivalent primary record confirming that commissioning has finished and the new plant has been handed over/entered normal operation. The planned 16 October 2026 community celebration is a future completion marker, not present proof of completion.
likely_source: Kempsey Shire Council Willawarrin WTP current-works page and project updates; commissioning/handover records; NSW Health/Department water-quality or section 60 records where publicly available.

question: What will the programmed Bellbrook WTP Augmentation (W3024-WF / G00241-01) actually deliver and when, and is Council's current Kempsey-source water-cartage contingency quantitatively adequate if Bellbrook and Willawarrin require emergency supply simultaneously?
why_exists: The project-existence and present contingency questions are now substantially answered. The adopted 2026-27 Operational Plan confirms Bellbrook WTP Augmentation W3024-WF / G00241-01 at $119,860 (EV-0095). Direct Council CEO correspondence conveying Utilities Directorate advice confirms the augmentation remains planned, Council intends to progress it, previous delivery was deferred due competing organisational priorities, and an internal Bellbrook site inspection is scheduled for mid-October 2026 (EV-0100). Council also confirms Bellbrook's primary source remains the local river and that water cartage from Kempsey is the current emergency contingency when that source is inadequate/unsuitable; in extended drought emergency supply may be drawn from Kempsey groundwater and Steuarts McIntyre Dam off-creek storage and carted to Bellbrook and Willawarrin (EV-0101). Council expressly confirms Willawarrin WTP is separate from Bellbrook (EV-0102). The unresolved issue is therefore not whether the Bellbrook project exists or whether Willawarrin is its backup: it is the augmentation's defined scope/timing/delivery and the demonstrated capacity of the stated emergency architecture under simultaneous demand.
evidence_required_to_resolve: Post-mid-October 2026 Bellbrook site-inspection outcome; defined W3024-WF / G00241-01 scope and design basis; 2026-27 deliverables and expenditure against the verified $119,860 allocation; procurement/construction/completion milestones; Bellbrook treatment-process gap analysis and Raw Water Catchment Category Assessment outputs; current Drought Management Plan/emergency supply procedure; and quantitative contingency evidence covering cartage triggers, Kempsey groundwater and Steuarts McIntyre Dam available drought yield, Bellbrook/Willawarrin demand and storage assumptions, tanker/logistics capacity, simultaneous-demand priority/continuity arrangements and expected cost. The correspondence establishes Willawarrin WTP is separate, so engineering evidence of an interconnection is no longer required to answer the current contingency unless Council later proposes one.
likely_source: Kempsey Shire Council Utilities Directorate; mid-October 2026 Bellbrook site-inspection record; Water Fund capital/project records; treatment-process gap and catchment assessment outputs; current Drought Management Plan/IWCM records; Kempsey drought-yield/storage and emergency-cartage operational records.

question: Why did the Willawarrin plant's projected cost rise from approximately $4 million (reported August 2024) to $8 million (reported March 2025), and what scope changes, if any, accompanied the increase?
why_exists: EV-0004 explicitly states the original 2024 projection was approximately $4 million and notes it was "since revised"; no source located explains the reason for the increase.
evidence_required_to_resolve: A council budget paper, tender documentation, or an officer's report explaining the revised cost estimate. RUN-0053 (2026-08-02): found the first source directly addressing this question - a National Water Grid Authority project page (SRC-0054/EV-0066) states Council "worked with the NSW Government's Safe and Secure Water Program to increase the value of the funding deed to accommodate cost increases from the competitive tender process." This points to pure cost escalation from the tender process (not an obviously described scope change) as the likely explanation, but remains search-snippet-only - a preserved primary document (a Council business paper, or the funding deed variation itself) is still needed to close this question with confidence.
likely_source: Kempsey Shire Council business papers or council meeting minutes from late 2024 or early 2025.

question: Is the change in Kempsey Shire Council Mayor between August 2024 (Leo Hauville, per EV-0004) and March 2025 (Kinne Ring, per EV-0005) attributable to the scheduled September 2024 NSW local government elections, or some other cause?
why_exists: Two evidence items from different dates name different individuals as Mayor. A routine election is the most plausible explanation but has not been separately confirmed by any evidence in this register.
evidence_required_to_resolve: A dated council governance record or NSW Electoral Commission result confirming the mayoral change and its cause.
likely_source: Kempsey Shire Council governance records; NSW Electoral Commission local government election results.

question: What contractor was awarded the main $52.9m Kempsey/Frederickton/Smithtown/Gladstone treatment plant (Steuart McIntyre Dam/Sherwood Borefield), and what is its construction status given the announced mid-2025 start and 18-month program (i.e. an implied completion around late 2026)?
why_exists: EV-0005 announces funding and a mid-2025-start, 18-month construction timeline for this larger, separate plant, but no contractor or progress information has yet been established by evidence in this register.
evidence_required_to_resolve: A tender award notice, construction-start announcement, or progress update for the main plant. RUN-0005 (2026-07-28) found a candidate answer - 'LC Eire, a partnership between LC Water and Eire Constructions' - repeated consistently across two independent search-engine snippets (SRC-0025, SRC-0026), but this has not been confirmed against either underlying article's primary text (both fetch-blocked this session, see DEC-0008), so it is not yet accepted as resolution evidence. RUN-0068 (2026-08-22): while re-sweeping this project's funding structure for any dated 2026 progress update, found a new, internally consistent but directly conflicting funding breakdown (National Water Grid Authority/DCCEEW project pages, corroborated by an Australian Pipeliner article dated 24 Mar 2025) - $17,225,000 NSW Government + $14.18m Kempsey Shire Council + a previously-unregistered $9m Australian Government Housing Support Program contribution, versus the $13.2m/$27.1m split already corroborated by three other independent dated sources (EV-0005, EV-0029, a 27 Mar 2025 Macleay Argus Mayor's column) - registered as EV-0075/CTR-0002. No new contractor or construction-progress information found; every search this run still surfaces only the already-registered LC Eire/12 ML per day/late-2026 figures.
likely_source: NSW Government (Water) / WaterNSW; Kempsey Shire Council; Utility Magazine (SRC-0025) or Mirage News (SRC-0026) once fetchable.

question: EV-0011 states the 2024 Kempsey Shire Council election results were 'for the September 9, 2024' poll, but multiple independent sources place the 2024 NSW Local Government elections' statewide polling day at Saturday 14 September 2024. Which is correct for Kempsey, and is EV-0011's date a simple error, a reference to a different date, or otherwise explainable?
why_exists: EV-0011 (a Kempsey Shire Council-bylined item) contains an internally curious date - 9 September 2024 was a Monday, inconsistent with the Saturday convention for NSW council elections and with general reporting on the 2024 statewide poll date. No independent source specific to Kempsey has yet been checked to confirm which date applies here; elections.nsw.gov.au (SRC-0018) is blocked to automated fetch.
evidence_required_to_resolve: The NSW Electoral Commission's own Kempsey Shire Council election results page or bulletin, confirmed by direct (manual) access. RUN-0011 (2026-07-28) adds a decisive, non-search basis pending a preservable primary citation: NSW ordinary council elections are legally required to fall on 'the second Saturday in September' (Local Government Act 1993, per SRC-0031's search-derived summary), and independently computed calendar facts (not search-dependent) confirm 14 September 2024 was both a Saturday and the second Saturday of that month, while 9 September 2024 was a Monday and not a Saturday at all. Combined with SRC-0029's independent search corroboration of 14 September as Kempsey's actual polling day, this makes EV-0011's '9 September 2024' very likely a simple transcription error for '14'. Not yet closing this question, since resolution_evidence requires a real preserved Evidence Register entry (the statute or an NSWEC bulletin), which remains fetch-blocked (DEC-0008). RUN-0046 (2026-08-02): found the NSW Electoral Commission's own dedicated past-results page for the Kempsey Shire Council mayoral election (SRC-0081/EV-0059), corroborated by a Kempsey-specific Macleay Argus report (SRC-0082) - both state the election was held Saturday 14 September 2024, and both cross-corroborate EV-0012's already-preserved 53.67%/30 September detail exactly. This is materially stronger than the prior statutory/calendar reasoning (Kempsey-specific rather than generic statewide), but is still search-snippet-only, not a fetched/preserved primary document, so this question remains formally Open pending an actual preserved copy of SRC-0081 or an equivalent primary record. RUN-0063: found a further Kempsey-specific corroboration - the Council's own 15 August 2024 ballot-draw article (SRC-0104) explicitly identifies 14 September 2024 as the polling day, alongside the 6 mayoral candidates. A third independent Kempsey-specific source now agrees with SRC-0081/SRC-0082, but remains search-snippet-only; still not sufficient to close this question under this investigation's established bar (a preserved primary document is required).
likely_source: elections.nsw.gov.au (SRC-0018, SRC-0029) or legislation.nsw.gov.au (SRC-0031) - both blocked to automated access, requires manual browser retrieval.

question: Why do Willawarrin and Bellbrook remain on standalone riverbank-bore extraction and local treatment, rather than being connected to (or given source redundancy through) the main Kempsey-Lower Macleay network that the Steuart McIntyre Dam / Sherwood Borefield plant serves?
why_exists: DFAPTA Cycle 1 (AR-018) noted that the main network can switch between the Sherwood Borefield and Steuart McIntyre Dam (EV-0005, EV-0028), while Willawarrin and Bellbrook remain single-source riverbank-bore systems with no documented redundancy. No options assessment, engineering feasibility study, or business case explaining this architecture choice has been located. The absence is analytically material because source architecture controls each village's exposure to drought, post-fire sediment, and turbidity.
evidence_required_to_resolve: A council engineering report, business case, or options assessment explicitly considering (and explaining the rejection or deferral of) pipeline connection or redundant source supply for Willawarrin and/or Bellbrook.
likely_source: Kempsey Shire Council water infrastructure strategy or asset management plan; council business papers from the SMD project's planning phase; NSW DCCEEW regional water strategy documents.

question: Where are the 2021-2022 and 2022-2023 Drinking Water Management System Annual Reports for Kempsey Shire Council, and why has the report series changed filename/URL convention three times (2018-2019, 2019-2021, 2023-2024 per EV-0065)?
why_exists: EV-0065 documents naming-convention and URL-pattern instability across the report series and an apparent two-year publication gap. This case's own evidentiary strength depends on being able to reconstruct the series continuously; an unresolved naming/access gap is itself an auditability problem regardless of whether the underlying cause is routine website restructuring.
evidence_required_to_resolve: Direct location of the 2021-2022 and 2022-2023 reports (or Council confirmation that no report was produced for those years and why), and a stable, current index page for the full report series. RUN-0071 (2026-08-24): located the 2022-2023 edition (EV-0076/SRC-0108), under a fourth, previously-untried naming convention ("dwms-annual-wq-report-2022-2023_v.1_final.1.pdf"). This closes half of the question - the 2021-2022 edition remains unlocated despite a further dedicated search this run trying the same naming convention and guessed variants for that year; still not found, and still not resolved to the point of a preserved primary document for the 2022-2023 edition either, since kempsey.nsw.gov.au remains fetch-blocked this session.
likely_source: Kempsey Shire Council's water and sewer publications page; NSW Health's Drinking Water Database (referenced but not directly queried in this case); a GIPA request if not publicly located.

question: What are LC Water's contractual acceptance criteria, commissioning obligations, and performance security terms for the Willawarrin plant, and does the contract specify a date by which commissioning must be complete?
why_exists: DFAPTA Cycle 1 (AR-012) found contractor identity well-supported (EV-0058, EV-0060) but noted the complete contract, tender evaluation, acceptance criteria, variation schedule, and handover obligations are not in the public corpus. This bears directly on Q-0001 (commissioning status): without the contract's own commissioning deadline, there is no independent benchmark against which the passed 'early 2026' target can be assessed as on-time, delayed, or within an agreed tolerance.
evidence_required_to_resolve: The executed contract or a Council summary of its key terms (commissioning date, acceptance criteria, liquidated damages or performance security provisions), likely only obtainable via a GIPA request given procurement contracts are not routinely published in full.
likely_source: Kempsey Shire Council contracts register (if published); a GIPA request to Council; Council business papers from the tender-award period (mid-2024).
